narrative: Demand for PL1__MFD8090A is strongly intermittent with only 40% of working days showing positive consumption and occasional large-batch events driving a CV of 2.07. Lead times are very short (mean 0.44 days) but volatile (CV 0.99), making demand variability the dominant buffer driver at 91% of total variance. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy is recommended with safety stock raised from 0 to 179 units to achieve the 95% service level target, and an EOQ-derived order quantity of 748 units to minimise total inventory costs. The optimised policy delivers an estimated 63.7% annual cost reduction versus the legacy zero-safety-stock SAP setting.
warnings: SAP safety stock is 0 — current ERP setting provides no stockout protection.
Lead time CV of 0.99 indicates high supplier delivery variability; monitor supplier performance closely.
Intermittent demand with CV > 2 may cause occasional over-ordering; review policy quarterly.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Intermittent zero-inflated demand with a short, volatile lead time favours a reorder-point trigger (r) over periodic review, as stock can deplete rapidly during active demand bursts. Fixed-quantity ordering (Q=EOQ) minimises the sum of ordering and holding costs and is straightforward to implement in SAP with a reorder-point MRP type.
research_insights.boundary_risk: No storage capacity constraint binds: SS(179) + OQ(748) = 927 units is well below the 6,591-unit limit. Primary service risk is the high demand intermittency — periods of zero demand followed by large spikes can cause the reorder point to be breached without warning; a daily stock-check cycle is recommended.
